evidence.observation: The reload options type exposes an optional `resolveProjectTrust` callback (line 37) that receives the pre-trust LoadExtensionsResult and returns the trust decision. Its presence is the single switch that enables the two-pass pre-trust/post-trust lifecycle; when it is undefined reload() runs a single flat pass.

The bootstrap (pre-trust) pass. It force-sets `settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(false)` and reloads settings, which clears project settings, so `loadCurrentExtensionSet({ includeInlineFactories: true })` (lines 606-633) loads only user/global extensions plus temporary CLI extension sources and inline factories. This is how project-local extensions/packages are deliberately kept out while still letting user/global and CLI extensions run to answer the trust prompt.

The lifecycle orchestrator. Lines 450-455 run the pre-trust half: capture `preTrustExtensions = await this.loadProjectTrustExtensions()` and pass it to `options.resolveProjectTrust`, then `this.settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(projectTrusted)` (line 454). Line 458 then reloads settings under the resolved trust state (the comment notes reload() preserves projectTrusted). Post-trust it resolves packages/CLI sources (459-505), loads the final extension set (512), and re-derives skills/prompts/themes/context files/system prompts (525-603). Every project-scoped resource is only folded in after this point.

The post-trust extension pass. When no pre-trust set exists it loads everything fresh (643-650). When a pre-trust set exists, it indexes the already-loaded extensions by resolvedPath and the failed preload paths (652-663), loads only the `remainingPaths` into the SAME runtime (`preTrustExtensions.runtime`, line 668), then re-orders the combined set to match the requested extensionPaths and appends inline factories (675-681). This guarantees user/global extensions are loaded once while newly-trusted project extensions are added on top.

Shared loader used by the pre-trust pass. It resolves packages and temporary CLI extension sources, merges them honoring `noExtensions`, collects host-provided dependency warnings, calls `loadExtensionsCached`, and (only when `includeInlineFactories` is true, as in the pre-trust pass) appends inline factory extensions. Because settings are untrusted at this point, `packageManager.resolve()` yields no project-local packages.

Project-resource discovery is trust-gated at the point of use: the project `SYSTEM.md` under cwd's config dir is only returned when `this.settingsManager.isProjectTrusted()` is true; otherwise it falls back to the global `SYSTEM.md` in agentDir. A parallel gate exists in `discoverAppendSystemPromptFile` (lines 1107-1119). These are called from reload() at lines 583-592, i.e. after the trust state has been set, so on an untrusted project the project prompt files are never read.

Post-trust context-file loading invoked from reload() at lines 572-579 (skipped entirely when `noContextFiles`). It loads the global agent-dir AGENTS/CLAUDE file first, then walks cwd and its ancestors, using `findShadowedContextFile` to suppress a main-repo context file that a nested linked worktree's copy shadows. Context files are gathered only in the post-trust phase, after `setProjectTrusted` has been applied and settings reloaded.

The decision function handed to reload()'s `resolveProjectTrust` hook (wired in main.ts:744-764). It resolves trust in a fixed precedence: explicit `trustOverride` (47-49); auto-true when `hasTrustRequiringProjectResources(cwd)` finds no trust-requiring project resources (50-52); a `project_trust` event emitted to the already-loaded pre-trust extensions (54-70), where a `{trusted:"yes"|"no"}` result can decide and optionally persist (`trustStore.set`) — this is why the pre-trust extension pass matters; then a stored trust-store decision (72-75); `defaultProjectTrust` always/never (77-84); finally an interactive UI select (86-94). With no UI it returns false (86-88), and it defaults to false if the prompt is dismissed (95).

The options shape shows the inputs the loader's hook supplies: cwd, trustStore, optional trustOverride and defaultProjectTrust, the `extensionsResult` (the pre-trust extension set used for the project_trust event), a projectTrustContext carrying UI access, and an onExtensionError callback used to surface project_trust event errors as warnings.

The interactive fallback: it obtains trust options via `getProjectTrustOptions(cwd, { includeSessionOnly: true })`, renders `formatProjectTrustPrompt`, and matches the UI selection back to a ProjectTrustOption. Its result is persisted by `saveProjectTrustPromptResult` (40-44) via `trustStore.setMany`, so the chosen scope (including session-only) is recorded before resolveProjectTrusted returns the boolean (lines 90-94).

claims.claim: reload() implements a two-pass lifecycle switched on the optional `resolveProjectTrust` option: the pre-trust pass deliberately forces the settings manager untrusted and loads only user/global plus temporary CLI extensions, then the resolved trust boolean is written back via setProjectTrusted and the SAME extension runtime is reused post-trust so already-loaded extensions are not re-executed.

resolveProjectTrusted resolves the project trust decision in strict precedence order — explicit override, the hasTrustRequiringProjectResources short-circuit to true, a project_trust event answered by the pre-trust extensions (optionally persisted), a stored trust-store decision, the defaultProjectTrust policy, and finally an interactive prompt — defaulting to false when no UI is available or the prompt is dismissed.

The two files form one contract: reload() in resource-loader.ts calls loadProjectTrustExtensions() to produce the pre-trust LoadExtensionsResult, passes it into the resolveProjectTrust callback, and main.ts wires that callback to resolveProjectTrusted() in project-trust.ts; project-trust.ts consumes that same extensionsResult to emit the project_trust event, which is the only reason project-local extension code must be excluded yet user/global extension code must be present before trust is decided.

Beyond extensions, project-scoped resources are trust-gated: the project SYSTEM.md / APPEND_SYSTEM.md are only discovered when isProjectTrusted() is true (otherwise the global agent-dir copies are used), and project context files (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) plus skills/prompts/themes are only materialized in the post-trust portion of reload(), after setProjectTrusted and the subsequent settings reload.

conclusion: The resource-loading lifecycle is a trust-gated two-pass pipeline anchored on DefaultResourceLoader.reload(). When a resolveProjectTrust hook is supplied, reload() first runs the pre-trust bootstrap (loadProjectTrustExtensions -> loadCurrentExtensionSet): it force-sets SettingsManager trust to false, reloads settings so project settings are cleared, and loads only user/global extensions, temporary CLI extension sources, and inline factories. That pre-trust LoadExtensionsResult is handed to the hook (in main.ts backed by resolveProjectTrusted in project-trust.ts), which decides trust via override -> no-trust-requiring-resources shortcut -> project_trust extension event -> stored decision -> defaultProjectTrust -> interactive prompt, defaulting to false without a UI. The returned boolean is applied with settingsManager.setProjectTrusted and a second settings reload, after which the post-trust half resolves project packages, loads only the not-yet-loaded extension paths into the reused runtime (loadFinalExtensionSet), and then loads project skills, prompts, themes, context files, and the trust-gated project SYSTEM.md/APPEND_SYSTEM.md. The effect is that untrusted project content never executes or loads during trust resolution, and trusted content is layered onto a runtime that already contains the user/global extensions needed to answer the trust prompt.
